outcome: Give development director / property operations head a governed method to improve weather-normalized energy intensity using BMS readings, occupancy and weather normalization, with final decisions…
overview: Building Energy Performance Benchmarking addresses telemetry is noisy or missing, so operators spend time interpreting unrelated warnings in construction and real estate operations. The first proof of value uses BMS readings, occupancy and weather normalization. It produces a reviewed operational recommendation and a traceable decision record. The commercial success measure is weather-normalized energy intensity, established from customer baseline data before any improvement is claimed.

scope:
Delivery model: Redington or approved implementation partner, eligibility and staffing pending confirmation.
Duration: Discovery and design first; pilot and rollout durations depend on data access and scope; no fixed commitment.
1) Discover source quality and baseline: BMS readings, occupancy and weather normalization; define weather-normalized energy intensity and data-processing boundary.
2) Design control points, security and connector contracts; obtain owner approval from Development Director / Property Operations Head.
3) Implement one bounded workflow, instrument missing-data exceptions and system-of-record write-back.
4) Test positive, negative, privilege, partial-data and rollback cases including inject sensor failures, stale data and dependency loss into the pilot.
5) Review KPI in the pilot, document evidence, perform training and agree transition.
